name: Ebola SEIR with intervention-time switch (Congo 1995 / Uganda 2000)
description:
Ebola virus disease, human.
The single structural feature that distinguishes this model is the step-then-exponential-decay transmission rate, implemented with ifelse on t.
Parameter values: 0 of 6 checked against the source; the rest are recalled or illustrative.
reference: Chowell G, Hengartner NW, Castillo-Chavez C, Fenimore PW, Hyman JM (2004). The basic reproductive number of Ebola and the effects of public health measures: the cases of Congo and Uganda. J Theor Biol 229(1):119–126

parameters.name: beta0
parameters.description: transmission rate before interventions (Congo 1995; 0.30 commonly quoted for Uganda 2000) [unverified] (per day)

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: exponential decay rate of transmission after interventions begin [unverified] (per day)

parameters.name: tau
parameters.description: day interventions begin (relative to epidemic start used in the fit) [unverified] (days)

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: rate of leaving latency (mean incubation 5.3 d) [unverified] (per day)

parameters.name: gamma
parameters.description: rate of leaving infectiousness (mean infectious period 5.61 d) [unverified] (per day)

parameters.name: cfr
parameters.description: proportion of infectious cases that die (Congo 1995; ≈0.53 Uganda 2000) [unverified] (dimensionless)

variables.name: beta_t
variables.expr: ifelse(t < tau, beta0, beta0 * exp(-q * (t - tau)))

variables.name: R0
variables.description: basic reproduction number (authors report ≈1.83 Congo 1995, ≈1.34 Uganda 2000) [unverified]

variables.name: CC_rate
variables.description: rate of new cumulative cases (bookkeeping for fitting to cumulative case curves) (integrate with cumsum for the cumulative count)
